messages:
Ethan: Quick Q after the all-hands: what's the single canonical place to point PMs about when to choose kernel work vs batching/caching?
Lina: We don't have one doc yet, so PMs keep pinging us. Good call to centralize.
Jun: TL;DR: kernels for deterministic tail and hardware-level wins; batching/caching for immediate cost wins and per-tenant tuning.
Ethan: Can we have some concrete numbers in that doc? PMs keep asking 'how much will this move p95 or cost'
Lina: We'll include ranges and recent examples. e.g., kernel fusion on attention gave ~12-18% P95 improvement for long-seq gen on A100s. Auto-batcher experiments gave ~15-25% cost reduction for high-concurrency chat flows.
Nadia: Also include example SLO impact: if you care about P99 < 250ms that pushes you toward kernel + placement; if your main ask is $/token for heavy embeddings, batching wins.
Ethan: Nice. Who owns the playbook?
Jun: Eng-runtime + Optimize should co-own. I'll volunteer eng-runtime to draft a skeleton.
Lina: Can we add a short checklist for private customers (on-prem)? They asked if they need reboots for kernel updates.
Jun: Most dedicated pools support live kernel swap, but some older on-prem images will need a rolling restart. We'll document which images are live-upgradeable.
Deploy Bot: deploy-bot initiated canary for kernel-fusion-v4 on pool:shared-eu at 1912346120 1% traffic.
Ethan: Can we make the playbook cover rollback steps? We had a botched rollout last quarter because folks couldn't flip a flag quickly.
Lina: Absolutely. Proposed rollback knobs: per-pool kernel selector, model+kernel pairing pin, and disabling the auto-batcher at runtime.
Nadia: Add a quick troubleshooting matrix: high CPU jitter, memory spikes, increased token error rates, stderr logs to grep.
Ethan: Can you paste the grep patterns? saves time for on-call.
Jun: Sure, gist of common checks:
```
# check kernel errors
sudo journalctl -u redwood-runtime | grep -i kernel
# check for kv cache misses
redwood-tools kv-stats --pool dedicated-us-west-2
# auto-batcher backpressure
curl -s http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep auto_batch_window
```
Lina: We'll include those in the playbook under "Ops quick checks".
Ethan: Product asked about expected timeline buckets: fast/typical/slow. Can we put numbers?
Jun: Proposal: fast = 1-2 weeks (config, batching rules), typical = 4-8 weeks (auto-batch tuning + small infra changes), slow = 2-4+ months (kernel impl + validation + driver tuning).
Nadia: Put a shrink-wrap note: kernel timelines vary by model family and QA surface area.
Deploy Bot: canary metrics update at 1912346200: latency p50 +2ms, p95 -9ms, error rate unchanged.
Ethan: Good signal. Who will be responsible for the communication thread to PMs/CS?
Lina: I'll draft an internal note and ping PM leadership. Jun can add the ops checklist.
Nadia: Add a short FAQ: "Will kernel changes affect cached completions?" Answer: usually no; logical KV prefixes are stable. If a kernel forces KV format bump we'll provide a migration tool.
Ethan: Any plan for automated risk scoring for proposals? e.g., small PR producing 0.5% p95 win but high risk isn't worth it.
Jun: We're prototyping a score combining expected impact, rollout risk, and verification cost. Early internal repo at https://phabricator.redwood/internal/kernels-risk (internal).
Lina: Action items: Jun to post draft by Wed, Lina to add PM-facing summary by EOW, Nadia to compile ops checks.
Ethan: One more ask from CS: a line for customers on Dedicated about downtime expectations.
Nadia: We'll state: "Most upgrades are live-swap; for older images a rolling restart may be required and will be scheduled with the customer."
SRE Bot: alert-sys: note: watch auto-batcher CPU contended on pool:shared-eu during canary window 1912346230.
Jun: Thanks SRE Bot 1 I'll watch the canary dashboard and post graphs to eng-runtime.
Ethan: Great. Please tag me when the doc is live so I can point PMs to it.
Lina: Will do. Closing thread once draft is up. :white_check_mark:
